thread:
matt: Customer reported duplicate charges after a tool call retry. Sending minimal repro + logs. Customer says two identical charge IDs were created within ~3s.

matt: Request payload (redacted):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-small-v1-tooling\",
  \"input\": \"charge  user\",
  \"tool_call\": {
    \"name\": \"charge_customer\",
    \"arguments\": {
      \"customer_id\": \"cus_ABC123\",
      \"amount\": 2500
    }
  }
}
```
(note: no Idempotency-Key header in these requests)

matt: Relevant log snippet (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-09T12:03:01Z] trace=tr_9f4a toolcall_attempt=1 exec_id=exe_01 external_http=POST /payments 200 body=\"{\"charge_id\":\"ch_01\"}\" result_schema_valid=false error=schema_validation_failed
[2026-03-09T12:03:03Z] trace=tr_9f4a toolcall_attempt=2 exec_id=exe_02 external_http=POST /payments 200 body=\"{\"charge_id\":\"ch_02\"}\" result_schema_valid=true status=ok
```
matt: Interpretation: tool actually executed twice. First run returned a 200 from the payments API, but the tool's response failed our JSON schema checks (we flagged result_schema_valid=false). The runtime considered the tool invocation unsuccessful and retried, re-invoking the tool which produced a second, valid charge. Customer was billed twice.

anna-oncall: Thanks — can you confirm route & retry policy? Is this on the hosted API path or Dedicated? Also paste request headers (esp Idempotency-Key).

matt: Hosted API, default route `generate` (no special side-effect policy). No Idempotency-Key header present in customer requests. Retry policy: runtime auto-retries transient tool failures up to 2 times. In this case the first tool returned an HTTP 200 but we treated the response as invalid because of schema mismatch. That triggered a retry.

jordan-runtime: That matches a pattern we've seen: if a tool returns syntactically/semantically invalid payload that fails our schema check, we currently classify the tool call as failed and will re-run. Problem: if the tool produced a side effect (HTTP call to external payments API), re-running causes duplicate side effects.

sasha-support: Customer is asking for a refund for ch_01 and wants root cause. Can billing refund and then we follow up on runtime fix? Marking P1 for now.

luis-billing: I need account id and charge IDs in the ticket. I'll start reversals once we have authorization. Please open a support case referencing this thread.

matt: Provided customer account `acct_ACCT99` and charge IDs `ch_01` and `ch_02`. Created ticket SUP-2026-137. Asking billing to prioritize.

jordan-runtime: Short-term mitigations we can apply server-side:
- Disable automatic retry for tool calls on routes flagged as possible side-effectful.
- Require/validate client-supplied Idempotency-Key for tool-executing routes and surface warning if missing.
- Persist tool exec results (including malformed results) with exec_id so retries can fetch instead of re-execute when possible.

anna-oncall: Which of these can we flip quickly? We should avoid a code change that might break behavior—maybe a config flag to turn off tool-call retries globally or per-customer.

jordan-runtime: I can push a config guard to disable retries for tool calls within 2-4 hours (feature flag). Longer-term patch: change retry logic to not re-invoke a tool if the tool returned a 200 and an exec_id was emitted — instead, surface a processing error and require manual reconciliation. That one needs an RFC.

sasha-support: Please enable the guard for this customer and add a notification to the account so teams are aware. Also add an automated suggestion to customers to include an `Idempotency-Key` header for any request that triggers an external side effect.

luis-billing: Proceeding with reversal for ch_01 after we validate the request. Will update SUP-2026-137.

ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-042 (link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-042)

jordan-runtime: One extra note: we found a related fallback path — if schema validation fails we sometimes fallback to non-tool completion (chat fallback) and then re-emit the tool call from the regenerated plan, which can cause another distinct execution. We'll include that in the RCA.

matt: Adding steps to reproduce in the ticket: 1) call API without Idempotency-Key, 2) have tool execute an external POST that returns a body that violates our declared schema, 3) observe retry + second exec_id + duplicate external side effect.

sasha-support: Thanks everyone. Action items: jordan - enable config guard + open RFC, luis - process refund, matt - keep customer updated, anna - monitor for other similar reports.

matt: Pinging here once guard is live. :pray:
